subject.title: feat(apps): review durable approvals on mobile

question: Should this PR preserve existing non-ASCII gateway TLS trust through an owner-verified migration, or intentionally require an explicit in-app re-trust flow?
rationale: The encoded account scheme prevents Unicode owner collisions, but the current migration guard makes previously stored non-ASCII pins disappear; choosing how trust is safely recovered is an upgrade and security-boundary decision.

options.title: Add verified migration
options.body: Migrate a raw legacy pin only when paired gateway state verifies its exact owner, preserving trust without ambiguous attribution.

options.title: Add explicit re-trust UX
options.body: Detect unavailable legacy trust and require a clearly explained in-app fingerprint confirmation rather than silently treating the gateway as unpinned.

options.title: Split storage hardening
options.body: Remove the TLS key migration from this approval increment and land it separately with dedicated upgrade and recovery proof.

recommendation.title: Add verified migration
recommendation.body: Migrate a raw legacy pin only when paired gateway state verifies its exact owner, preserving trust without ambiguous attribution.

likelyOwner.reason: The strongest current-main ownership signal covers the mobile gateway, TLS storage, and stacked durable-approval direction.
